key_insight: In forced stably stratified turbulence, interface merging is linked to the emergence of vertically sheared helical structures that break mirror symmetry and drive vertical drift.
engineering_relevance: Understanding when stratified layers coarsen or remain stable helps predict mixing, interface transport, and long-time evolution in geophysical and industrial flows.
method: Direct Numerical Simulations of forced stably stratified turbulence
Moderate-resolution runs with very long temporal integration
Comparison across different Froude numbers to distinguish drift/merging from decay
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that at Fr = 0.076 the simulations show kinetic-energy excursions and vertical interface drift/merging, while at Fr = 0.22 the helical structures are absent and interfaces decay instead.
watch_item: The conclusions come from moderate-resolution DNS, so the mechanism should be checked for sensitivity to resolution, forcing details, and broader parameter ranges.
paper_title: Drift of interfaces in forced stably-stratified turbulence and the role of vertically-sheared helical structures
